question: Which Chinese traveller visited India during the reign of Harshavardhana?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Hsuan Tsang.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Hsuan Tsang (Xuanzang) was a Chinese Buddhist monk and traveller who visited India during the reign of Harshavardhana (606-647 CE). (ह्वेनसांग — हर्षवर्धन के शासनकाल में भारत आया)

 

• He stayed in India for about 14 years (c. 630-644 CE), studied at the Nalanda University, and left a detailed account of the political and social conditions of India titled 'Si-Yu-Ki' (Records of the Western World).

 

• He attended Harsha's religious assembly at Kannauj and the quinquennial (every five years) distribution of alms at Prayag.

 

• He is regarded as one of the most important sources for reconstructing the history of Harsha's reign and the Nalanda Mahavihara.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Harshavardhana ruled from 606-647 CE, established his capital at Kannauj, and authored plays like Ratnavali, Priyadarshika and Nagananda.

 

NOTE

 

• Etsing (Option 2): A Chinese Buddhist monk who visited India later, in the second half of the 7th century, mainly to study at Nalanda; his account is 'A Record of the Buddhist Religion'.

 

• Faxian (Option 3): A Chinese monk who visited India much earlier, during the reign of Chandragupta II (c. 399-414 CE), not Harsha.

 

• Ibn Battuta (Option 4): A Moroccan traveller who visited India during the reign of Muhammad bin Tughlaq in the 14th century, not a Chinese traveller.

question: Thomas Cup is a/an________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is biennial event.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Thomas Cup is the world men's team badminton championship, held once every two years (biennially). (थॉमस कप — द्विवार्षिक आयोजन)

 

• It is organised by the Badminton World Federation (BWF) and was first held in 1948-49.

 

• It is named after Sir George Alan Thomas, a former president of the International Badminton Federation.

 

• India won the Thomas Cup for the first time in 2022, defeating Indonesia in the final held in Bangkok, Thailand.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The women's equivalent of the Thomas Cup is the Uber Cup, also held every two years, in the same years and often at the same venue as the Thomas Cup.

 

NOTE

 

• Annual event (Option 1): Incorrect; the Thomas Cup is not held every year.

 

• Quarterly event (Option 3): Incorrect; it is not held four times a year.

 

• Triennial event (Option 4): Incorrect; it is not held once every three years.

question: 'Penalty Corner' is related to which of the following sports?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Hockey.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A Penalty Corner is a scoring opportunity awarded to the attacking team in field hockey for certain rule infringements by the defending team inside the 'D'/circle. (पेनल्टी कॉर्नर — हॉकी)

 

• It is also called a 'short corner' and is a common way of scoring goals, especially through drag-flicks.

 

• Field hockey terminology also includes 'long corner', 'penalty stroke' and 'bully' (an older method of restarting play).

 

• India has a strong hockey heritage, having won multiple Olympic gold medals and hosting major tournaments like the Hockey World Cup.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The national governing body for hockey in India is Hockey India, and the sport's global body is the International Hockey Federation (FIH).

 

NOTE

 

• Chess (Option 1): Uses terms like check, checkmate, castling, and stalemate — not penalty corner.

 

• Tennis (Option 2): Uses terms like deuce, ace, and love — not penalty corner.

 

• Badminton (Option 3): Uses terms like smash, rally, and let — not penalty corner.

question: Which is the only living representative of Sphenopsida that has an underground, creeping and perennial rhizome that gives off aerial as well as underground branches?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Equisetum.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Equisetum (commonly called horsetail) is the only living genus of the class Sphenopsida (Equisetopsida) among pteridophytes. (इक्विसीटम — स्फेनॉप्सिडा का एकमात्र जीवित वंश)

 

• It has an underground, creeping, perennial rhizome from which both aerial branches (jointed, ribbed stems) and underground branches arise.

 

• The stem is characteristically jointed and hollow, with whorls of scale-like leaves at each node, and the plant reproduces through spores borne in strobili (cones).

 

• Sphenopsida is one of the classes of Pteridophyta, along with Psilopsida, Lycopsida and Pteropsida.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Pteridophytes are vascular cryptogams — they possess vascular tissue but reproduce via spores, not seeds, and include ferns, horsetails and club mosses.

 

NOTE

 

• Adiantum (Option 1): A genus of ferns (maidenhair fern) belonging to class Pteropsida, not Sphenopsida.

 

• Dryopteris (Option 2): Also a true fern belonging to class Pteropsida.

 

• Selaginella (Option 3): Belongs to class Lycopsida (club mosses), not Sphenopsida.

question: Trichloromethane is better known as:
solution_text:
The correct answer is chloroform.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Trichloromethane (CHCl₃) is the chemical/IUPAC name for the common compound chloroform. (ट्राइक्लोरोमीथेन — क्लोरोफॉर्म)

 

• Chloroform is a colourless, sweet-smelling, dense liquid historically used as an anaesthetic and as a solvent in laboratories and industry.

 

• It contains one carbon atom, one hydrogen atom and three chlorine atoms per molecule, hence the name 'tri-chloro-methane' (methane with three hydrogens replaced by chlorine).

 

• It is no longer used medically as an anaesthetic due to its toxic and carcinogenic effects, but remains important as an industrial solvent and in the production of refrigerants.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Common name-formula pairs: Nitrous oxide (N₂O) = laughing gas; LPG = mixture of butane and propane; Methane (CH₄) is the simplest hydrocarbon.

 

NOTE

 

• Butanes (Option 2): Refers to the hydrocarbon C₄H₁₀, not trichloromethane.

 

• LPG (Option 3): Liquefied Petroleum Gas, a mixture mainly of butane and propane, unrelated to trichloromethane.

 

• Laughing gas (Option 4): The common name for nitrous oxide (N₂O), not trichloromethane.

question: Which Constitutional Amendment added Fundamental Duties in the Constitution?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Forty-Second Amendment Act, 1976.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976 added a new part, Part IVA (Article 51A), laying down Fundamental Duties of citizens, based on the recommendations of the Swaran Singh Committee. (42वां संविधान संशोधन — मूल कर्तव्य)

 

• Originally 10 Fundamental Duties were added; the 86th Amendment Act, 2002 added an 11th duty relating to providing opportunities for education to children aged 6-14 years.

 

• The 42nd Amendment is also known as the 'Mini-Constitution' because of the sweeping changes it made, including amendments to the Preamble (adding 'Socialist', 'Secular', 'Integrity').

 

• It was enacted during the Emergency period (1975-77) under the government of Indira Gandhi.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Fundamental Duties are inspired by the Constitution of the erstwhile USSR and, like the Directive Principles, are non-justiciable (not enforceable by courts).

 

NOTE

 

• Forty-Seventh Amendment, 1984 (Option 2): Related to land reform laws being placed under the Ninth Schedule, not Fundamental Duties.

 

• Forty-Fourth Amendment Act, 1978 (Option 3): Restored several changes made by the 42nd Amendment and removed the Right to Property as a Fundamental Right (making it a legal right under Article 300A).

 

• Fifty-Second Amendment, 1985 (Option 4): Introduced the Anti-Defection Law via the Tenth Schedule.

question:
Match the columns.

States : Hills

1. Kerala : a. Anaimalai Hills

2. Meghalaya : b. Garo Hills

3. Mizoram : c. Lushai Hills
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1-a, 2-b, 3-c.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Kerala - Anaimalai Hills; Meghalaya - Garo Hills; Mizoram - Lushai Hills is the correct matching. (अनाईमलाई पहाड़ियाँ — केरल, गारो पहाड़ियाँ — मेघालय, लुशाई पहाड़ियाँ — मिज़ोरम)

 

• The Anaimalai Hills (part of the Western Ghats) lie in Kerala and Tamil Nadu and are home to Anamudi, the highest peak in South India.

 

• The Garo Hills are located in western Meghalaya and form part of the Meghalaya Plateau along with the Khasi and Jaintia Hills.

 

• The Lushai Hills (also called the Mizo Hills) form most of the hill ranges of Mizoram.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Meghalaya is often called the 'abode of clouds'; its three main hill ranges are Garo, Khasi and Jaintia Hills.

 

• Anamudi peak (Anaimalai Hills, Kerala) has an elevation of about 2,695 metres, the highest in Peninsular India.

 

NOTE

 

• Options 2, 3 and 4 are incorrect because they mismatch one or more state-hill pairings against the correct list given above.

question: Vijayanagara emperor Krishnadeva Raya founded a suburban township near Vijayanagara called Nagalapuram after his _________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is mother.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Krishnadevaraya, the great Vijayanagara ruler, founded the suburban township of Nagalapuram near the capital in memory of his mother, Nagalamba (Nagala Devi). (नागलपुरम — कृष्णदेवराय की माता के नाम पर)

 

• Krishnadevaraya belonged to the Tuluva dynasty of the Vijayanagara Empire and ruled from 1509 to 1529 CE.

 

• He was a great patron of art, literature and architecture, and his court housed the Ashtadiggajas, eight eminent Telugu poets, including Allasani Peddana.

 

• He also authored the Telugu work 'Amuktamalyada'.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Krishnadevaraya's reign is considered the golden age of the Vijayanagara Empire; he defeated the Sultan of Bijapur and expanded the empire's territory significantly.

 

• Portuguese travellers Domingo Paes and Duarte Barbosa visited his court and left detailed accounts of Vijayanagara.

 

NOTE

 

• Father (Option 1): Nagalapuram was not named after his father, Narasa Nayaka.

 

• Teacher (Option 2): It was not named after a teacher/guru.

 

• Sister (Option 3): It was not named after a sister.

question: How many nominated members are there in the Legislative Assembly of Telangana?
solution_text:
The correct answer is One.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Telangana Legislative Assembly provides for one nominated member from the Anglo-Indian community, as historically permitted under Article 333 of the Constitution. (तेलंगाना विधानसभा — एक मनोनीत सदस्य)

 

• This provision mirrored the one for the Lok Sabha and other state assemblies, under which the Governor could nominate one Anglo-Indian representative if the community was inadequately represented.

 

• Telangana became India's 29th state on 2 June 2014, formed by bifurcation of Andhra Pradesh.

 

• The Telangana Legislative Assembly otherwise has 119 elected members.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The 104th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2019 discontinued the reservation and nomination of Anglo-Indian members in the Lok Sabha and state assemblies with effect from 25 January 2020, though the seat continued to exist in Telangana beyond that date until vacated.

 

NOTE

 

• Four, Two, Three (Options 1, 3, 4): Incorrect; the Telangana Assembly's provision was for only one nominated member, not two, three or four.

question: On International Women's Day 2022, the Ministry of MSME launched an entrepreneurship drive for women by which of the following names?
solution_text:
The correct answer is SAMARTH.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• On International Women's Day, 8 March 2022, the Ministry of MSME launched the 'SAMARTH' - Special Entrepreneurship Promotion Drive for Women. (समर्थ — महिला उद्यमिता संवर्धन अभियान)

 

• It was launched by the then Union MSME Minister Shri Narayan Rane.

 

• The drive aimed to promote entrepreneurship among women by connecting them with various MSME schemes such as PMEGP, CGTMSE and PSU procurement benefits.

 

• It was implemented through 150 Special Camps across the country and coordinated with State/UT MSME departments.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other women-centric welfare schemes of the Government of India include Ujjawala (anti-trafficking) and Swadhar Greh (support for women in difficult circumstances), both under the Ministry of Women and Child Development.

 

NOTE

 

• NIRBHAYA (Option 2): Refers to the Nirbhaya Fund, set up for women's safety initiatives, not an MSME entrepreneurship drive.

 

• SWADHAR (Option 3): A Ministry of Women and Child Development scheme for rehabilitation of women in difficult circumstances, not an MSME scheme.

 

• UJJAWALA (Option 4): A Ministry of Women and Child Development scheme against trafficking and for rescue of victims, not an MSME scheme.

question: What are the main energy sources for earth's internal heat engine?
option_1: Radiogenic heat and oceanic tide heat
option_2: Heat from volcanoes and solar heat
option_3: Solar heat and oceanic tide heat
solution_text:
The correct answer is Radiogenic heat and primordial heat.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Earth's internal heat engine is driven mainly by two sources: radiogenic heat (from radioactive decay of elements like uranium, thorium, and potassium) and primordial heat (residual heat retained from the planet's formation and core differentiation). (भू-आंतरिक ऊष्मा — रेडियोजेनिक व प्रारंभिक ऊष्मा)

 

• This internal heat drives processes such as mantle convection, plate tectonics, volcanism and the geodynamo that generates Earth's magnetic field.

 

• Radiogenic heat is generated continuously within the Earth's crust and mantle due to the decay of radioactive isotopes.

 

• Primordial heat dates back to the Earth's accretion (~4.5 billion years ago) from the kinetic energy of colliding planetesimals and the gravitational energy released during core-mantle differentiation.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Earth's internal structure consists of the crust, mantle, outer core and inner core; heat flows outward from the core through the mantle to the crust via convection and conduction.

 

NOTE

 

• Options 1, 2 and 3 are incorrect because solar heat and oceanic tide heat are external, surface-level energy sources (affecting climate and tides) and are not sources of the Earth's internal heat engine; volcanoes are a manifestation of internal heat, not a source of it.

question: Select the correct statement about the achievements of Sruti Bandopadhay, an eminent Manipuri dancer.
option_1: She received Padma Shri for the year 2020.
option_2: She received Sangeet Natak Akademi Award for the year 2020.
option_3: She received Kalidas Samman for the year 2020.
option_4: She received Padma Vibhushan for the year 2020.
solution_text:
The correct answer is She received Sangeet Natak Akademi Award for the year 2020.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Dr. Sruti Bandopadhyay is a renowned exponent, choreographer and guru of Manipuri dance, and the founder-director of the Dansha Academy, Kolkata. (श्रुति बंद्योपाध्याय — मणिपुरी नृत्य)

 

• She was conferred the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award for the year 2020 for her contribution to Manipuri dance.

 

• The Sangeet Natak Akademi Award is the highest national recognition given to practising artists in the fields of music, dance and drama in India, conferred by the Sangeet Natak Akademi, the country's national academy for performing arts.

 

• She has also worked extensively on choreography, dance research and training of students in the Manipuri dance tradition.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Manipuri dance is one of the eight classical dance forms of India, known for its graceful movements and association with Ras Lila performances depicting the life of Krishna and Radha.

 

NOTE

 

• Padma Shri for 2020 (Option 1): She was not conferred the Padma Shri for that year.

 

• Kalidas Samman for 2020 (Option 3): She did not receive the Kalidas Samman (a Madhya Pradesh government award) for that year.

 

• Padma Vibhushan for 2020 (Option 4): She did not receive the Padma Vibhushan, which is a higher civilian award, for that year.

question: Which of the given personalities is NOT associated with Carnatic Music?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Vishnu Narayan Bhatkhande.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Vishnu Narayan Bhatkhande was a pioneering musicologist associated with Hindustani classical music, not Carnatic music. (विष्णु नारायण भातखंडे — हिंदुस्तानी शास्त्रीय संगीत)

 

• He is credited with systematising Hindustani classical music into ten thaats (parent scales) and founded institutions like the Marris College of Music (now Bhatkhande Sangeet Vidyapeeth), Lucknow.

 

• In contrast, MS Subbulakshmi was a legendary Carnatic vocalist, the first musician to be awarded the Bharat Ratna.

 

• Subramania Bharathiyar, the noted Tamil poet, was also closely associated with Carnatic music compositions, and Kalyani Varadarajan is known as a Carnatic musician/veena player.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Carnatic music system is prevalent mainly in South India, while the Hindustani system is prevalent in North India; both share common roots in ancient Indian musical traditions.

 

NOTE

 

• Kalyani Varadarajan (Option 1): A Carnatic musician, hence associated with Carnatic music.

 

• MS Subbulakshmi (Option 2): A celebrated Carnatic vocalist and Bharat Ratna awardee.

 

• Subramania Bharathiyar (Option 4): A Tamil poet whose works are widely set to and sung in the Carnatic tradition.

question: Which of the following Acts was introduced to regulate Foreign Exchange in India in 1973?
solution_text:
The correct answer is FERA.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Foreign Exchange Regulation Act (FERA) was enacted in 1973 to regulate certain payments, dealings in foreign exchange and securities, and transactions affecting the foreign exchange market in India. (विदेशी मुद्रा विनियमन अधिनियम — 1973)

 

• FERA was a stringent, conservation-oriented law enacted at a time of foreign exchange scarcity, and violations under it were treated as criminal offences.

 

• It was replaced by the more liberal Foreign Exchange Management Act (FEMA), 1999, in line with India's economic liberalisation policies, with violations under FEMA treated as civil offences.

 

• FERA came into force from 1 January 1974.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• FEMA, 1999 came into effect from 1 June 2000 and is administered by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) and the Directorate of Enforcement.

 

NOTE

 

• FEMA (Option 2): Enacted in 1999, replacing FERA; not the 1973 Act.

 

• FRBM (Option 3): The Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management Act, 2003, deals with fiscal deficit management, not foreign exchange.

 

• SARFESI (Option 4): The Securitisation and Reconstruction of Financial Assets and Enforcement of Security Interest Act, 2002, deals with recovery of bad loans by banks, not foreign exchange regulation.

question: Which of the following dances is performed by the Santhal tribe of Jharkhand?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Jhika Dasain.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Jhika Dasain is a famous tribal dance predominantly performed by the Santhal tribe of Jharkhand, typically during festive occasions. (झीका दसाईं — संथाल जनजाति, झारखंड)

 

• The Santhal are one of the largest tribal communities of India, found mainly in Jharkhand, West Bengal, Odisha and Bihar.

 

• Other important dances of the Santhal and related tribal communities of Jharkhand include Karam, Jhumar/Jhumair, Domkach, Paika and Chhau.

 

• Jharkhand's tribal dances are typically accompanied by traditional instruments like the madal (drum), tamak and flute, and are performed during harvest and seasonal festivals.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Chhau dance, a semi-classical martial dance form of Jharkhand, Odisha and West Bengal, has been inscribed on UNESCO's Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity.

 

NOTE

 

• Kolkali (Option 2): A folk dance associated with Kerala (Malabar region), not Jharkhand.

 

• Ghumar (Option 3): A traditional folk dance of Rajasthan, not Jharkhand.

 

• Koli (Option 4): A folk dance of the Koli fishing community of Maharashtra, not Jharkhand.

question: Which of the following cell organelles is made up of ribosomal RNA and protein?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ribosome.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Ribosomes are cell organelles composed of ribosomal RNA (rRNA) and proteins, and are the sites of protein synthesis in the cell. (राइबोसोम — राइबोसोमल आरएनए व प्रोटीन)

 

• They occur as two subunits — a large subunit and a small subunit — which join together during translation.

 

• Ribosomes are found either freely in the cytoplasm or attached to the endoplasmic reticulum (forming the rough endoplasmic reticulum), and also occur in mitochondria and chloroplasts.

 

• Prokaryotic cells have 70S ribosomes, while eukaryotic cells have 80S ribosomes.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Ribosomes were first observed by George Palade in 1955 using an electron microscope, for which he later received the Nobel Prize.

 

NOTE

 

• Nucleus (Option 2): The membrane-bound organelle containing the cell's genetic material (DNA), not made of rRNA and protein.

 

• Golgi body (Option 3): Involved in modifying, packaging and transporting proteins and lipids; composed of membrane-bound sacs (cisternae), not rRNA and protein.

 

• Lysosome (Option 4): A membrane-bound organelle containing digestive enzymes, not composed of rRNA and protein.

question: Shri Sagar Kailas Ovhalkar was in news for being conferred with Arjuna Award 2022 for his outstanding contribution in which of the following sports?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mallakhamb.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Sagar Kailas Ovhalkar, a mechanical engineer from Mumbai, was conferred the Arjuna Award 2022 for his outstanding contribution to Mallakhamb. (सागर कैलास ओव्हाळकर — मल्लखंभ)

 

• He became the first Indian man to receive the Arjuna Award for Mallakhamb.

 

• He has won gold medals in Pole Mallakhamb events (Long Set and Small Set) at the World Championships, 2019.

 

• The Arjuna Award, instituted in 1961, is given by the Government of India for outstanding achievement in sports.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Mallakhamb is a traditional Indian sport in which a gymnast performs feats and poses in concert with a vertical wooden pole, cane, or rope; it originated in Maharashtra and has ancient roots described in the 12th-century text Manasollasa.

 

NOTE

 

• Kabaddi, Chess, Judo (Options 1, 2, 3): Sagar Kailas Ovhalkar was recognised for his contribution to Mallakhamb, not any of these sports.

question: Who among the following was the first person to discuss poverty line in pre-independent India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Dadabhai Naoroji.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Dadabhai Naoroji was the first to conceptualise and discuss the poverty line in pre-independent India, in his book 'Poverty and Un-British Rule in India' (1901). (दादाभाई नौरोजी — निर्धनता रेखा की अवधारणा)

 

• He calculated a 'national minimum income' required for a person to subsist, based on the cost of a subsistence diet, and used it to estimate the extent of poverty in India under British rule.

 

• He is also famous for propounding the 'Drain of Wealth' theory, explaining how British policies drained India's wealth to Britain.

 

• He was popularly known as the 'Grand Old Man of India' and was the first Indian to be elected to the British House of Commons.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Later poverty estimation methods in independent India were developed by economists and committees such as the Working Group (1962), VM Dandekar and Nilakantha Rath, and the Alagh Committee (1979).

 

NOTE

 

• Mahalanobis (Option 2): PC Mahalanobis was a statistician known for the Mahalanobis model used in India's Second Five-Year Plan, not the first to discuss the poverty line.

 

• Dr. BR Ambedkar (Option 3): Chief architect of the Indian Constitution; not credited as the first to discuss the poverty line.

 

• RK Shanmukham Chetty (Option 4): India's first Finance Minister, who presented independent India's first Union Budget; not associated with first discussing the poverty line.

question: Identify the group of states that are covered in the Sardar Sarovar Project.
option_1: Maharashtra, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh and Jharkhand
option_2: Maharashtra, Madhya Pradesh, Gujarat and Rajasthan
solution_text:
The correct answer is Maharashtra, Madhya Pradesh, Gujarat and Rajasthan.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Sardar Sarovar Project, built on the Narmada River, is a multi-purpose project benefiting the four states of Gujarat, Maharashtra, Madhya Pradesh and Rajasthan. (सरदार सरोवर परियोजना — गुजरात, महाराष्ट्र, मध्य प्रदेश, राजस्थान)

 

• The dam itself is located in Gujarat (Narmada district), near Navagam, and it is one of the largest dams in India.

 

• It provides irrigation, drinking water and hydroelectric power to the beneficiary states; the Statue of Unity, dedicated to Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, is located near this dam.

 

• The project has been a subject of the long-running Narmada Bachao Andolan, an environmental and social movement.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Narmada river originates from the Amarkantak Plateau in Madhya Pradesh and flows westward into the Arabian Sea through the Gulf of Khambhat.

 

NOTE

 

• Options 1, 3 and 4 are incorrect because they include states like Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, Punjab, Haryana, Karnataka and Telangana, which are not part of the Sardar Sarovar Project's beneficiary states.

question: Which German chemist and physicist proposed that an aromatic compound must have an odd number of pairs of electrons, Which can mathematically be written as 4n+2 (n = 0,1,2,3, etc.) in 1931?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Erich Huckel.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Erich Huckel, a German chemist and physicist, proposed Huckel's Rule in 1931, stating that a planar, cyclic, fully conjugated compound is aromatic if it has (4n+2) π electrons, where n = 0, 1, 2, 3, etc. (एरिक हकल — 4n+2 नियम, 1931)

 

• This rule is a cornerstone of organic chemistry for predicting the aromaticity of cyclic compounds, such as benzene (n=1, 6 π electrons).

 

• Huckel developed this rule using molecular orbital theory (Huckel Molecular Orbital theory).

 

• Compounds satisfying (4n+2) π electrons are termed aromatic, while those with 4n π electrons in a similar cyclic, planar, conjugated system are termed anti-aromatic.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Benzene (C₆H₆), with 6 π electrons (n=1), is the classic example of an aromatic compound explained by Huckel's Rule.

 

NOTE

 

• Friedrich Kekule (Option 1): German chemist known for proposing the cyclic ring structure of benzene, not Huckel's Rule.

 

• Rosalind Franklin (Option 2): British scientist known for her X-ray diffraction work contributing to the discovery of the DNA double helix structure, unrelated to aromaticity rules.

 

• Antoine Lavoisier (Option 4): French chemist known as the 'Father of Modern Chemistry', credited with the law of conservation of mass, not Huckel's Rule.

question: Under whom was CP Ilbert a law member of the council?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Lord Ripon.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• CP Ilbert (Sir Courtenay Peregrine Ilbert) served as the Law Member of the Governor-General's Council under Lord Ripon, the Viceroy of India from 1880 to 1884. (सी.पी. इल्बर्ट — लॉर्ड रिपन के अधीन विधि सदस्य)

 

• He is best known for drafting the Ilbert Bill (1883), which sought to allow Indian judges/magistrates to try British/European offenders in criminal cases — a proposal that caused strong opposition (the 'Ilbert Bill controversy' or 'White Mutiny') from the European community in India.

 

• The bill was eventually passed in a modified/diluted form in 1884, allowing European defendants the right to claim a jury with at least half European members.

 

• Lord Ripon is also remembered for introducing local self-government through the Resolution on Local Self-Government, 1882, and is often called the 'Father of Local Self-Government in India'.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Lord Ripon also repealed the Vernacular Press Act, 1878, restoring freedom to the Indian language press.

 

NOTE

 

• Lord Lytton (Option 1): Viceroy known for the Vernacular Press Act, 1878 and the Second Anglo-Afghan War, not associated with the Ilbert Bill.

 

• Lord Cornwallis (Option 2): Known for the Permanent Settlement (1793) in Bengal, much earlier than Ilbert's tenure.

 

• Lord Curzon (Option 4): Known for the Partition of Bengal (1905), not associated with CP Ilbert.

question: Who among the following is the author of the book 'The Buddha and his Dhamma', which appeared in 1957 after the death of its author?
solution_text:
The correct answer is BR Ambedkar.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Dr. BR Ambedkar authored the book 'The Buddha and His Dhamma', which was published posthumously in 1957, a year after his death in December 1956. (द बुद्ध एंड हिज़ धम्म — डॉ. बी.आर. आंबेडकर)

 

• The book presents Ambedkar's interpretation of Buddhism and was written towards the end of his life, reflecting his conversion to Buddhism in October 1956 at Nagpur (Deekshabhoomi).

 

• Ambedkar is also renowned as the chief architect of the Indian Constitution and the first Law Minister of independent India.

 

• He was posthumously awarded the Bharat Ratna in 1990.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Ambedkar's other notable works include 'Annihilation of Caste' and 'The Problem of the Rupee'.

 

NOTE

 

• Subhas Chandra Bose (Option 1): Known for founding the Indian National Army (INA); not the author of this book.

 

• Mahatma Gandhi (Option 3): Known for works such as 'My Experiments with Truth' (autobiography); not the author of this book.

 

• Motilal Nehru (Option 4): Known for the Nehru Report (1928); not the author of this book.

question: Nag Panchami is celebrated in which month of Hindu Calendar?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Shravan.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Nag Panchami is a traditional Hindu festival dedicated to the worship of snakes/serpent deities (Nagas), celebrated on the fifth day (Panchami) of the bright fortnight (Shukla Paksha) of the month of Shravan. (नाग पंचमी — श्रावण मास)

 

• Shravan (also spelt Sawan) usually falls in July-August as per the Gregorian calendar, and is considered a highly auspicious month in Hinduism, also associated with fasting (Shravan somwar) and Shiva worship.

 

• On this day, devotees offer milk, and worship images or idols of snakes, seeking protection from snakebites and the blessings of Nagas.

 

• The festival has particular significance in states like Maharashtra, Rajasthan, Karnataka, and parts of North India.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other major Shravan month festivals include Raksha Bandhan and Hariyali Teej.

 

NOTE

 

• Kartik (Option 2): Associated with festivals like Diwali and Kartik Purnima, not Nag Panchami.

 

• Sharad (Option 3): Associated with the autumn season and festivals like Sharad Purnima, not Nag Panchami.

 

• Asadh (Option 4): Associated with festivals like Rath Yatra, not Nag Panchami.

question: __________ became the first swimmer from India to breach the Olympic Qualification Time (A cut) in swimming as he capped the qualification period with an outstanding performance in the Sette Colli Trophy in Rome, Italy in June 2021.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sajan Prakash.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Sajan Prakash became the first Indian swimmer to achieve the Olympic 'A' qualifying time, doing so at the Sette Colli Trophy in Rome, Italy, in June 2021 in the men's 200m butterfly event. (सजन प्रकाश — भारत के पहले 'ए' कट तैराक)

 

• This achievement earned him direct qualification for the Tokyo 2020 Olympics (held in 2021), making him only the second Indian swimmer (after Khajan Singh in 1956) to qualify for the Olympics without a wild card entry, based purely on his timing.

 

• Sajan Prakash hails from Kerala and has represented India in multiple international swimming events, including the Asian Games and Commonwealth Games.

 

• He has also been a recipient of national swimming honours and continues to be one of India's leading swimmers.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Sette Colli Trophy is an annual international swimming meet held in Rome, Italy.

 

NOTE

 

• Srihari Nataraj (Option 2): A notable Indian swimmer (backstroke specialist) but not the swimmer who achieved this particular 'A cut' milestone in 2021.

 

• Anand Anilkumar Shylaja (Option 3): An Indian swimmer, but not associated with this particular first.

 

• Virdhawal Khade (Option 4): A well-known Indian swimmer and Arjuna Awardee, but not the one who achieved this specific 'A cut' milestone at the 2021 Sette Colli Trophy.

question: Who is the regulator of Micro Finance Institutions in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is RBI.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) is the primary regulator of Micro Finance Institutions (MFIs) in India, particularly those registered as Non-Banking Financial Company-Micro Finance Institutions (NBFC-MFIs). (आरबीआई — सूक्ष्म वित्त संस्थानों का नियामक)

 

• RBI issues regulatory guidelines covering aspects such as capital adequacy, interest rate caps, lending limits, and qualifying assets for NBFC-MFIs.

 

• In 2022, RBI introduced a new regulatory framework for microfinance loans, applicable uniformly to all regulated entities engaged in microfinance lending.

 

• RBI is the central bank of India, established in 1935, and also regulates banks and NBFCs more broadly.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• NABARD plays a supporting/developmental role for microfinance (e.g., through the SHG-Bank Linkage Programme), but the direct regulatory authority over MFIs/NBFC-MFIs rests with the RBI.

 

NOTE

 

• SEBI (Option 1): Regulates the securities market in India, not microfinance institutions.

 

• NABARD (Option 3): Focuses on agricultural and rural development finance and supports microfinance through refinancing, but is not its primary regulator.

 

• SBI (Option 4): A public sector commercial bank, not a regulatory authority.
